root_causes.description: The frontend container was terminated ('Killing: Stopping container frontend') and immediately replaced by a freshly scheduled pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8, causing the frontend server request rate to collapse (p50 ~8 req/s vs. a window mean of ~148 req/s). Error rate and CPU on the frontend pods stayed normal, indicating a container-level crash/restart rather than a resource or downstream fault.

evidence.observed_value: request_rate mean=148.190 req/s, p50=8.009 req/s (collapse), p95=432.873, max=604.823; anomaly flagged

evidence.expected_baseline: no container-stop/kill events during steady state

evidence.observed_value: new frontend pod created and started (Scheduled/Created/Started events count=1 each)
evidence.expected_baseline: no pod rescheduling/replacement in steady state

evidence.observed_value: restarts mean=0.000, max=0.000 (replacement pod freshly started, counter reset)

root_causes.description: A downstream propagation hypothesis (frontend depends on checkout) is plausible if the frontend request collapse were caused by an upstream dependency, but frontend error_rate stayed flat (~0.006) and no checkout-side anomaly was observed, making this a weaker secondary explanation.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate mean=0.006 (no spike), inconsistent with a downstream dependency failure

root_causes.description: A latency-based fault was considered, but the observed anomaly was a request-rate collapse plus a container-kill event while CPU and error signals remained flat, so latency saturation is an unlikely root cause.

remediation_steps: Confirm the frontend pod restart/crash: kubectl -n otel-demo get pods -l app=frontend and kubectl describe pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8 (inspect Last State, Reason, Exit Code).
Inspect the terminated frontend container's previous logs (kubectl logs <prior-frontend-pod> --previous) to distinguish OOMKill, liveness-probe kill, or application crash.
Check frontend resource limits/requests and liveness/readiness probe thresholds; raise memory/CPU limits or tune probe timeouts if the container was killed by resource pressure or a failed probe.
Verify load-generator traffic recovery by confirming frontend request_rate returns to its ~148 req/s baseline after the replacement pod is Ready.
